DEV-01_feeOnTransferBufferOverCredit.claimA: buffer credited 100,000e18 vs actual custody 95,000e18 — accounting exceeds custody immediately.
DEV-01_feeOnTransferBufferOverCredit.claimB: Two pairs of the SAME token: sum of buffers 200,000e18 vs pooled custody 190,000e18. Pair A settles first and is paid its full over-stated buffer (streamer pays out 100,000, A nets 95,000); the streamer is left with 90,000 against pair B's 100,000 claim, and B's pullPendingStream REVERTS. Cross-pair drain CONFIRMED.
DEV-01_feeOnTransferBufferOverCredit.claimC: A clean token settles fine in isolation, but the tainted token's pullPendingStream reverts — and batchMint loops pullPendingStream over getNudgeTokens() in ONE transaction, so one tainted token bricks the whole mint path. CONFIRMED.
DEV-01_feeOnTransferBufferOverCredit.claimD: With fee set to 0 the divergence vanishes entirely — the DeployMocks probe at :1661 passes vacuously, exactly as MockKendu guarantees. CONFIRMED.
DEV-01_feeOnTransferBufferOverCredit.notesOnNatSpec: NudgeStreamer.sol:194-196 asserts 'The buffer cap guarantees the streamer can never transfer more than it holds, even if elapsed is large.' That guarantee is PER-STREAM while custody is POOLED PER-TOKEN, so it does not hold across pairs. Test B falsifies it directly.

DEV-03_zeroStreamerGuardAsymmetry.poc: workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevStreamerWiring.t.sol (run with --fork-url against the live local chain)
DEV-03_zeroStreamerGuardAsymmetry.finding: All SIX donor contracts REJECT setNudgeStreamer(address(0)) — BalancerPoolerV2, NudgeRatchet, UniboostEYE/SCX/FLX, StableYieldAccumulator. BatchNFTMinterMultiToken ACCEPTS it silently (no guard at BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:299-302).
DEV-03_zeroStreamerGuardAsymmetry.consequenceProved: With the sink's streamer wired, a qualifying batchMint pays the batcher 45,045,015 USDC + 5,000e18 phUSD + 50,000e18 Kendu. With the sink's streamer zeroed, the SAME batchMint SUCCEEDS — no revert, no event — and pays 189,464 USDC + 0 phUSD + 0 Kendu, leaving the entire matured pot stranded in the streamer.
DEV-03_zeroStreamerGuardAsymmetry.correctsPriorClaim: This REFUTES the handed-over FIND-2 mechanism. FIND-2 claimed a mainnet script sourcing NudgeStreamer from the 0x0 placeholder would wire setNudgeStreamer(address(0)) on BalancerPoolerV2 and have the resulting _psmDonate revert swallowed by _dispatch's try/catch. Empirically, BalancerPoolerV2.setNudgeStreamer REVERTS on address(0) (BalancerPoolerV2.sol:247) — the mis-wire fails LOUDLY at deploy time. The genuinely silent path is the batch-minter sink, which is the one setter with no guard.

DEV-04_donationSwallowIsBoundedNotSilent.finding: BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch's `try this._psmDonate{} catch` DOES emit DonationSkipped(remainingUSDS) (:291-293), and the swept USDS PARKS on the pooler and is re-swept by the next dispatch (:287-289, documented :56-60). So a swallowed donation is observable and recoverable, not lost value.
DEV-04_donationSwallowIsBoundedNotSilent.correctsPriorClaim: FIND-2's 'donation vanishes silently, no event' is wrong on both counts. The residual real risk is operational quietness (the operator must watch DonationSkipped and the pooler's USDS balance), not value loss.
